entities.summary:
Sétna Airt, son of Artrí, son of Éber, son of Ír, son of Míl Espáine, was a High King of Ireland. He came to power after the death of Rothechtaid mac Main, whom he killed in single combat at Cruachan, fighting to protect his son, Fíachu Fínscothach. He ruled for five years, until Fíachu, returning from exile, killed him at Cruachan.

Sétna Airt's reign was marked by a struggle for power with his nephew Fíachu, who eventually succeeded him. The conflict between the two High Kings had significant consequences for the kingdom, leading to a period of instability and power struggles.

Despite his tumultuous reign, Sétna Airt's legacy endured, with his son Fíachu going on to found the Fíanchad dynasty, which would rule Ireland for centuries to come.

Sétna Airt's story is a testament to the complexities and intrigues of ancient Irish politics, where personal feuds and power struggles often shaped the course of history.

As the High King of Ireland, Sétna Airt played a crucial role in the kingdom's development, shaping its politics, culture, and identity in lasting ways.

In the annals of Irish history, Sétna Airt's name is often remembered alongside that of his son Fíachu, whose dynasty would go on to shape the course of Irish history for generations to come.

This High King's story is one of the most fascinating and complex in Irish mythology, offering a glimpse into the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined ancient Irish politics.

Sétna Airt's reign was a pivotal moment in Irish history, marking a turning point in the struggle for power between the different High Kings and setting the stage for the conflicts that would shape the kingdom for centuries to come.

The legend of Sétna Airt serves as a reminder of the enduring power of family, loyalty, and ambition in shaping the course of human history.
